fluff.overview: As with the Angel Light Strike Fighter, the Defender Medium Strike Fighter has become a universal standard in middleweight conventional fighters since its debut in the days of the Star League. The Defender was first introduced by Imstar Aerospace of Amity for planetary air garrisons across the Free Worlds League, particularly those with less funding. An aggressive interstellar sales program and the openness of the Star League gave Imstar room to sell these affordable defense assets across the Inner Sphere, whether in the form of actual constructed airframes or specifications and licenses to duplicate them. Powered by reliable Imstar-C 150 air-breathing turbines and armed with a mix of short- and long-ranged missiles, the Defender filled a critical niche for garrison forces unable to afford aerospace fighters.
fluff.capabilities:
The Defender achieves excellent airspeed for a conventional craft, enough to overtake or outrun a Planetlifter or Mekbuster. As an atmospheric fighter, it is also far more adept at in-atmosphere dogfighting than aerospace fighters with the same thrust capabilities, though it remains quite fragile compared to such fighters. This combination of speed and maneuverability with an arsenal of short- and long-ranged missiles makes the Defender an ideal choice for engaging other conventional fighters, VTOLs, or ground targets, while also providing a relatively inexpensive support craft for engaging low-flying aerospace units.

The Defender's armament centers on a nose-mounted Irian Weapon Works SRM 2 backed by two wing-mounted LongFire LRM 5 launchers. This mix allows the Defender to engage targets at multiple ranges, opening with long-range missile volleys before closing for a short-range strike. The Riese Heavy armor provides more protection than many conventional fighters in its weight class, though it remains far short of what even the lightest aerospace fighter can carry. The Lassitor 2JA communications system and IMB SYS 3000 targeting suite round out a reliable if unspectacular electronics package that has the virtue of being easy to maintain and replace with locally sourced components.
fluff.deployment: Owing to a production boom in the Star League era and the subsequent Succession Wars, the Defender became a widespread design. This fighter was produced across the Inner Sphere under a variety of names but almost always the same performance profile and general configuration, overtaking competitors, even aerospace fighters, simply because it was easy to build with the technology found on the average planet rather than some advanced subcontracting factory now destroyed or isolated by shortages of JumpShips. House Steiner became one of the biggest users during the later Succession Wars, deploying both standard and variant models of these strike fighters to many border worlds as part of an effort to strengthen previously low-priority garrisons.
fluff.history:
During the Second Succession War, Lockheed/CBM of Gibbs introduced a carrier-launched version of the Defender locally dubbed the Kaiseradler (roughly "Imperial Eagle") for use by Lyran air defense forces. This variant reduced its fuel capacity by one ton but added VSTOL capabilities ideal for short runways and carrier landings, and traded its armament for two wing-mounted TharHes Blue SRM 4 racks and a pair of Kicker machine guns. To offset its range disadvantages, the Kaiseradler was often paired with unmodified Defenders produced locally as the Steinadler ("Golden Eagle").

The Capellan Confederation produced its own Defender variant, the Crane, at Mujika Aerospace Technologies on St. Ives alongside the venerable Guardian. This model carries a third five-tube LRM launcher in place of the nose-mounted SRM and links all three launchers into a single ammunition bin. The resulting fighter has improved hitting power at long range, enough to endanger most other conventional fighters with even a single volley.

After rediscovering Artemis IV fire-control technology in 3035, engineers in the Free Worlds League developed one of the first lostech upgrades for a conventional fighter by installing the system on their Defenders in 3038, producing the Defender II. This variant drops the nose-mounted SRM in favor of Artemis fire control upgrades for the wing-mounted LRMs. While this slightly reduces short-range potential, the Defender II enhances effectiveness against more distant targets and would again become a Sphere-wide standard, supplanting the original Defender on production lines across the Inner Sphere.
